title: Locally, a stratum of a constructible partition is closed with quasi-compact complement
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme and $Y= igsqcup_{
u=1}^N Y_
u$ a finite partition of its underlying set into pairwise disjoint subsets, each locally closed [def-weil-locally-closed-subset] and constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Let $y\in Y$ and let $k$ be the index with $y\in Y_k$. Then there is an affine open subscheme $V\subseteq Y$ with $y\in V$ such that: (1) $Y_k\cap V$ is closed in $V$; (2) for every $
u$ the set $Y_
u\cap V$ is locally closed and constructible in $V$; (3) the open subset $V\setminus(Y_k\cap V)$ is quasi-compact.

proof.text: Because $Y_k$ is locally closed, write $Y_k=W\cap Z$ with $W$ open and $Z$ closed. We have $y\in W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], applied to the scheme $Y$, the open $W$ and $y\in W$, choose an affine open $V$ with $y\in V\subseteq W$. Then $Y_k\cap V=Z\cap V$ is closed in $V$ by the subspace topology.

proof.text: The complement $C=V\setminus(Y_k\cap V)$ is open by Step 1 and constructible in $V$ by Step 2 and the Boolean-complement clause of [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Since $V$ is an affine scheme, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] makes it quasi-compact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-is-retrocompact] to the topological space $V$ and its constructible subset $C$: the whole space $V$ is a quasi-compact open test subset, so $C\cap V=C$ is quasi-compact.
